posts.author: elonmusk
posts.text:
Gavin Baker owned 15% of Nvidia and 10% of Tesla before either was worth $2 billion. He’s 50. And he just admitted Claude Code was too hard for him, so he switched to Grok Bot.

“I glued together all this stuff with Claude Code and, you know, I’m sure it was user error on my part. 50 years old. I’m doing my best.”

Then he tried Grok Bot.

“Grok Bot is the most impactful AI product to me and to the firm that we’ve had yet.”

“It just makes it so easy. I think I’m up to like 17 Grok Bots, and every day I think of a new one to add.”

And it’s not a toy for him. It’s how he runs money:

“For the more professional use cases, Grok Bot has just been transformative for me.”

“So much of investing is making sure that the right information gets to the right person at the right time, and Grok Bot is so good at that.”

One of the best tech investors alive runs his firm on 17 AI agents. And he’s adding a new one every day.

Communists make disgusting anti-beauty art, but classical liberals aren’t like that. Put the libs in charge of the coffee shops, put the conservatives in charge of city hall. This is how you get a city that is beautiful, clean, and functional.

posts.text:
Here's some fuel for all the Europoor haters:

Germany just told us we'd have to fire one of our 3 founders to qualify for funding.

I was in talks with a German state-backed fund of fund managing billions, with one single mandate: invest in German funds to drive innovation and economic growth in the country.

They literally told me they like us a lot and are also impressed by our track record and performance so far, and even though not everyone in their team is a fan of our thesis, they believe in it.

But they passed for a whole different reason:

Because our all-male team of 3 people isn't "diverse enough" lol.

they literally told me: hire two more female partners (impossible on the economics of a fund our size), or let one of the three of us go to make room for a quota hire. do that, and they'd strongly consider investing.

I won't even get into how discriminatory this is toward men in the first place. nobody takes that seriously anyway, and honestly I don't care.

but what actually gets me is something bigger: as a German, I have to face the fact that the whole world continuing to laugh at Germany and overall Europe is completely justified.

a system that quietly kills the smallest, hungriest teams, the exact ones this money was created to support. and then everyone acts surprised that talent and capital keep leaving the country.

posts.text:
When computers and robots advance enough, legacy governance will look awkwardly quaint.

If they can build almost everything, why can't residents submit proposals, vote on them, and have them built?

Instead of years of theater, projects can be completed in days.

Want a high-speed railway? It costs X joules and hours to construct and Y joules per day to operate, with options A, B, and C. The full blueprint is attached for verification. No endless fake tax-raising campaign to fund something that does not exist. You pay with the electricity bill. No additional income or property taxes. Obviously, places with cheap electricity would have more build-out than places that don’t.

Once started, every agent can access the real-time status.

It may seem like fantasy, but the technology is almost there.

posts.author: elonmusk
posts.text:
It’s time to put all the pieces together, the early tests to see how crazy it was to build a vehicle this size, the suborbital hops to practice subsonic maneuvering, the first real booster, expendable flight tests, trips to the Indian Ocean, and last flight with payload to orbit. We are one step away from the full mission, and that step is the double catch.

We will try for the first time on flight 15. I don’t think and of us can promise it will work the first time, but getting here feels like a turning point. I still feel like there’s so much to review (and we will be doing that continuously between now and launch) but when I take a moment to stop and think about it, it is overwhelmingly exciting. This is the rocket that will build a human civilization on another planet.

quote.author: firesidealpha
quote.name: Fireside Alpha
quote.text:
SpaceX’s Arizona data center, per a county supervisor: “We could be reducing property taxes across the board in Cochise County, the entire county, by 20%”

Frank Antenori, whose district includes the site, brought up the county’s tax math during a live Q&A:

“Here’s just something to just chew on. Arizona has an expenditure limit requirement that is placed on counties. If we exceed that expenditure, we have to rebate back to the taxpayers a certain amount.”

“So, if we’re receiving revenue in from SpaceX, by law, we have to offset that to the taxpayers. We have the potential to reduce, based on the projected revenue they’re creating, as much as 20%.”

“Let me just say it again. We could be reducing property taxes across the board in Cochise County, the entire county, by 20% to offset for the revenue here, because we can’t spend all that money. So, we have to give that money back to the taxpayers. The law says we have to.”

“So, you could see a potential significant impact to local property taxes. What that is, I don’t know. We’re going to have to do the math on it. But the law, if we have this large increase in property tax revenue, we have to balance those rates. So that will reduce dramatically the property tax burden of every resident in the county.”

“The construction sales tax, which also is the TPT, the transaction privilege tax, the retail tax, and the jail excise tax. So that will be part of the construction tax. We could literally use that money to pay the jail off in 2 to 3 years, as opposed to the 13 to 20 years.”

“So this could be a revenue to eliminate the half-cent sales tax in 2 to 3 years. We can get rid of that half-cent sales tax.”
